title: Mick's analysis: FLIR1 object is a distant aircraft and its 'zip off' is camera movement

tellings.quote: Fleer one in particular uh was deemed to be amazing because the object appears to zip off screen
video and um one of them he hypothesizes that it's a a distant airliner. I think you said on a a podcast that it's probably 50 to 100 miles away.
tellings.difference: Told by Merrick about Mick's YouTube video. It specifies an airliner 50 to 100 miles away but does not mention the 'zip off' being camera movement.
tellings.link_reason: Both are Mick West's analysis that the FLIR1 object is a distant aircraft; this telling describes his video making that case.

as_told.title: Mick's video calling the FLIR1 object a distant airliner

related.note: An analysis of the same FLIR1 footage that concludes it shows a Tic Tac-shaped craft, against telling 6's distant aircraft.
This explains the same FLIR1 object as a balloon, while the existing story calls it a distant aircraft. These are competing core claims about one object.

plain: The skeptic researcher Mick West argues that the object in FLIR1, a 2004 Navy infrared video of the Tic Tac (a white oval object shaped like the mint, filmed off Southern California), is a distant aircraft, and that the moment it seems to "zip off screen", which made the clip look "amazing", is really the camera moving. In the same debate the writer Marik von Rennenkampff sums up West's YouTube analysis as saying the object is probably a distant airliner "50 to 100 miles away", though his version leaves out the point about camera movement. If West is right, one of the best-known Navy UFO videos would show an ordinary plane.
